info.title: Cross-platform Go CLI syscall module setup

diffs.patch:
Index: Makefile
===================================================================
--- Makefile	
+++ Makefile	
@@ -0,0 +1,37 @@
+BINARY := syscli
+DIST := dist
+VERSION ?= $(shell git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo dev)
+LDFLAGS := -s -w -X main.version=$(VERSION)
+
+PLATFORMS := linux/amd64 linux/arm64 darwin/amd64 darwin/arm64 windows/amd64 windows/arm64
+
+.PHONY: all build test vet fmt clean dist release
+
+all: build
+
+build:
+	go build -trimpath -ldflags "$(LDFLAGS)" -o $(BINARY) .
+
+test:
+	go test ./...
+
+vet:
+	go vet ./...
+
+fmt:
+	gofmt -l -w .
+
+clean:
+	rm -rf $(BINARY) $(DIST)
+
+dist:
+	@mkdir -p $(DIST)
+	@for p in $(PLATFORMS); do \
+		os=$${p%/*}; arch=$${p#*/}; \
+		ext=""; \
+		if [ "$$os" = "windows" ]; then ext=".exe"; fi; \
+		echo "building $$os/$$arch"; \
+		GOOS=$$os GOARCH=$$arch CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -ldflags "$(LDFLAGS)" -o $(DIST)/$$os-$$arch/$(BINARY)$$ext . || exit 1; \
+	done
+
+release: dist

Index: internal/sysinfo/uptime_darwin.go
===================================================================
--- internal/sysinfo/uptime_darwin.go	
+++ internal/sysinfo/uptime_darwin.go	
@@ -0,0 +1,18 @@
+//go:build darwin
+
+package sysinfo
+
+import (
+	"time"
+
+	"golang.org/x/sys/unix"
+)
+
+func Uptime() (time.Duration, error) {
+	tv, err := unix.SysctlTimeval("kern.boottime")
+	if err != nil {
+		return 0, err
+	}
+	boot := time.Unix(tv.Sec, int64(tv.Usec)*int64(time.Microsecond))
+	return time.Since(boot), nil
+}

Index: internal/sysinfo/uptime_linux.go
===================================================================
--- internal/sysinfo/uptime_linux.go	
+++ internal/sysinfo/uptime_linux.go	
@@ -0,0 +1,17 @@
+//go:build linux
+
+package sysinfo
+
+import (
+	"time"
+
+	"golang.org/x/sys/unix"
+)
+
+func Uptime() (time.Duration, error) {
+	var si unix.Sysinfo_t
+	if err := unix.Sysinfo(&si); err != nil {
+		return 0, err
+	}
+	return time.Duration(si.Uptime) * time.Second, nil
+}

Index: internal/sysinfo/uptime_windows.go
===================================================================
--- internal/sysinfo/uptime_windows.go	
+++ internal/sysinfo/uptime_windows.go	
@@ -0,0 +1,19 @@
+//go:build windows
+
+package sysinfo
+
+import (
+	"time"
+
+	"golang.org/x/sys/windows"
+)
+
+var procGetTickCount64 = windows.NewLazySystemDLL("kernel32.dll").NewProc("GetTickCount64")
+
+func Uptime() (time.Duration, error) {
+	if err := procGetTickCount64.Find(); err != nil {
+		return 0, err
+	}
+	ms, _, _ := procGetTickCount64.Call()
+	return time.Duration(ms) * time.Millisecond, nil
+}

Index: main.go
===================================================================
--- main.go	
+++ main.go	
@@ -0,0 +1,45 @@
+package main
+
+import (
+	"encoding/json"
+	"flag"
+	"fmt"
+	"os"
+	"time"
+
+	"example.com/syscli/internal/sysinfo"
+)
+
+var version = "dev"
+
+func main() {
+	if err := run(); err != nil {
+		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "syscli:", err)
+		os.Exit(1)
+	}
+}
+
+func run() error {
+	asJSON := flag.Bool("json", false, "encode output as JSON")
+	showVersion := flag.Bool("version", false, "print version and exit")
+	flag.Parse()
+
+	if *showVersion {
+		fmt.Println(version)
+		return nil
+	}
+
+	info, err := sysinfo.Collect()
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+
+	if *asJSON {
+		return json.NewEncoder(os.Stdout).Encode(map[string]float64{
+			"uptime_seconds": info.Uptime.Seconds(),
+		})
+	}
+
+	fmt.Println(info.Uptime.Round(time.Second))
+	return nil
+}

Let me understand the task. The user wants to set up a new Go module for a CLI tool that needs low-level system calls not exposed by the standard library on Linux, macOS, and Windows.

The key phrase: "low-level system calls not exposed by the standard library". Since Go 1.4+, the standard library's `syscall` package is frozen. For low-level syscalls, the recommended approach is `golang.org/x/sys/unix` for Unix (Linux, macOS) and `golang.org/x/sys/windows` for Windows.

So the module structure should include:
- `go.mod`
- A `main.go` for the CLI
